paper.title: Petition style changes with AI writing support but outcomes do not improve
paper.abstract: Nature Human Behaviour, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41562-026-02579-1 In 2023, Change.org introduced an artificial intelligence (AI)-supported petition-drafting tool to their platform. With access to this tool, users’ petitions changed substantially, and their texts became more similar to one another. At the same time, overall petition outcomes did not improve, which shows the limits of AI integration into online advocacy communities.

script.description_en: In 2023, Change.org added an AI tool that helps users draft petitions. A new study in Nature Human Behaviour finds that petitions changed substantially and became more similar to each other once users had the tool, yet overall outcomes did not improve. AI can change how advocacy sounds without changing what it achieves.
script.method_summary: The study examined Change.org, an online petition platform that introduced an AI-supported petition-drafting tool in 2023. The researchers compared petitions written by users with access to this tool against petitions written without it (around the tool's introduction), using computational text analysis to measure how petition texts changed and how similar petitions were to one another. They also compared petition outcomes. According to the published abstract, two main findings emerged: first, with access to the AI tool, users' petitions changed substantially and their texts became more similar to one another (a homogenizing effect on writing). Second, overall petition outcomes did not improve. The authors interpret this as showing the limits of integrating AI into online advocacy communities: AI writing support altered style and reduced diversity of texts, but did not translate into better results for petitioners on the whole. The abstract does not specify the sample size, the exact outcome measures, the specific text-similarity method, or effect sizes, so these details were not reported in this episode.
script.limitations: Based on the abstract alone, exact sample size, outcome metrics, and effect sizes are not stated, so no numbers were reported. The study covers a single platform, Change.org, so results may not generalize to other platforms, countries, or forms of advocacy. 'Outcomes did not improve' refers to overall results; it does not show that AI never helps an individual petition, nor does it fully explain why outcomes stayed flat (e.g., whether homogenized texts cancel each other out). Design details limiting causal claims are not described in the abstract.

pt.title: IA escreveu o abaixo-assinado. Ele ganhou mais?
pt.paper_title: Ferramentas de IA mudam a escrita de petições online, mas não seus resultados
pt.description: Em 2023, a Change.org lançou uma ferramenta de IA que ajuda os usuários a redigir abaixo-assinados. Um novo estudo na Nature Human Behaviour mostra que, com a ferramenta, os textos mudaram bastante e ficaram mais parecidos entre si, mas os resultados gerais não melhoraram. A IA pode mudar o jeito como o ativismo soa, sem mudar o que ele conquista.

script.description_zh: 巴西有些養牛牧場被查出奴役勞工，政府和企業紛紛制裁。但制裁之後業者怎麼反應，過去幾乎沒有證據。這篇PNAS研究用數百萬筆牛隻交易紀錄補上這塊空白，發現業者不是收手，而是以「洗白」和「規避」換方式繼續。
script.description_en: Some ranches in Brazil's cattle industry were caught using slave labor, and governments and companies moved to sanction them. But there has been almost no evidence on how sanctioned operators actually respond. This PNAS study fills that gap with millions of cattle transaction records, documenting laundering and evasion instead of simply stopping.
script.method_summary: The study (Mittelberg, Skidmore, Brandão, Rausch and Gibbs; University of Wisconsin–Madison and University of Illinois; PNAS 2026) asks how perpetrators of modern slavery in Brazil's cattle sector change their behavior after antislavery sanctions. Its key contribution: governments and companies have worked to rid supply chains of modern slavery, but little was known about policy outcomes, especially how perpetrators respond to sanctions. The authors use data on millions of cattle transactions in Brazil, which record cattle moving between properties and buyers, effectively forming a network of cattle flows. They examine the transactions of operators sanctioned under antislavery policies and how their selling behavior changes in response. The paper's title identifies two behavioral responses: laundering (making cattle linked to sanctioned operators appear clean as they move through the supply chain) and evasion (adjusting behavior to avoid the consequences of sanctions). The core message is that sanctioned actors adapt rather than simply stopping, which matters for designing supply-chain monitoring. Only the abstract's opening was available to us, so specific effect sizes, sample counts, the exact identification strategy, and how prevalent each response is were not provided and are not stated in the video.
script.limitations: We only had a truncated abstract, so the video gives no effect sizes or prevalence figures. Transaction records only capture recorded sales; informal or unrecorded movements of cattle are invisible. The analysis is observational, so behavior changes are associated with sanctions rather than proven to be solely caused by them. The study focuses on Brazil's cattle sector and may not generalize to other countries or commodities, and it does not show which policy fixes would work best.

script.description_zh: 很多公司宣布徵才不再要求大學學歷，但沒學歷的人真的因此被錄取了嗎？Lyttelton等人把徵才廣告和美國人口普查薪資紀錄連起來，追蹤2011到2021年。被錄取的非大學勞工一年多賺約4600美元，但雇主拿掉門檻後其實很少錄取他們。
script.description_en: Many employers say they no longer require a college degree, but do non-college workers actually get those jobs? Lyttelton and colleagues linked job postings to US Census earnings records from 2011 to 2021. Non-college workers hired into decredentialed jobs earned about $4600 more a year, yet employers rarely hired them after dropping the requirement.
script.method_summary: Thomas Lyttelton, Dylan K. Nelson and Nathan Wilmers, in Nature Human Behaviour (2026), studied 'decredentialing': employers dropping college-degree requirements from job postings. They linked job postings data to US Census Bureau earnings records covering 2011 to 2021. This linkage let them identify jobs whose postings dropped degree requirements and connect those jobs to the workers hired into them, including whether those workers lacked a college degree, and to their earnings. Main findings as reported in the abstract: non-college workers who were hired into jobs that had dropped degree requirements earned around US$4600 more per year, suggesting such jobs can be a path to upward mobility. However, employers rarely hired non-college workers after decredentialing, meaning that removing the requirement on paper did not usually translate into actually hiring people without degrees. The video only describes the study at the level of detail available in the abstract; exact linkage procedures, sample sizes and comparison groups are not stated there.
script.limitations: Based on the abstract only, details such as sample size, how postings were matched to employers and workers, and what comparison group defines the $4600 gain are not available. The earnings difference should not be read as a guaranteed causal effect for any individual. The study covers the USA from 2011 to 2021 and may not generalize to other countries or periods. It does not explain why employers rarely hired non-college workers after dropping requirements.

paper.title: The Effects of Generative AI on Collaboration and Social Networks Among Knowledge Workers
paper.abstract: The rapid diffusion of generative artificial intelligence has raised concerns that knowledge work may become less dependent on human-to-human interaction. Yet because AI-generated outputs require interpretation, verification, and social legitimation, generative AI may instead increase collaboration among workers. We test these competing predictions using passively collected behavioral data from more than 12,000 knowledge workers observed over 13 months during the staged organizational rollout of an AI-powered assistant (Microsoft Copilot). Using two complementary quasi-experimental designs -- a staggered difference-in-differences model and a fixed-effects instrumental-variable approach -- we estimate the effects of generative AI on workers' collaboration behavior and social network structure. We estimate that generative AI increased collaboration time across communication channels and reshaped individual networks. Those using generative AI interacted with more colleagues and their networks became less clustered, indicating broadening in collaboration structures. At the same time, they also concentrated more of their collaboration on ties with stronger prior histories, deepening reliance on already trusted colleagues. Together, these findings suggest that, while generative AI changes how people work, it may not displace human-to-human interactions.

script.description_zh: Apple要把AI聊天機器人加進Pages、Keynote和Numbers，AI助理進了辦公室，同事還重要嗎？博科尼大學團隊分析一家跨國公司一萬兩千多名員工13個月的會議、通話、郵件紀錄，發現開始用Copilot的人合作時間變多、接觸更多同事，同時也更依賴原本信任的老同事。研究只涵蓋一家公司、採用後頭三個月。
script.description_en: Apple is adding an AI chatbot to Pages, Keynote, and Numbers, so does an office AI assistant make us need coworkers less? A Bocconi University team analyzed 13 months of meeting, call and email logs from over 12,000 employees at one multinational firm during a staged Copilot rollout. Adopters collaborated more, reached more colleagues, and leaned harder on trusted ones. The study covers one company and the first three months after adoption.
script.method_summary: The authors used passively collected Microsoft Viva Insights data on 12,040 employees in one business unit of a large multinational consumer-products company, observed monthly from September 2024 to September 2025 during a staged rollout of Microsoft Copilot. Collaboration was measured from logs of meetings, calls, emails and chats; Copilot use was logged by a separate system as monthly actions. Each month they built a directed, weighted collaboration network, keeping ties of at least about one hour. Three network measures: out-degree (number of distinct people a worker reaches), clustering (how much a worker's contacts know each other), and preferential reinforcement (correlation between current time with each contact and past cumulative time). Adoption was defined as exceeding the 25th percentile of use for two consecutive months; after dropping 172 always-adopters, 1,992 adopters were compared with 9,876 never-adopters using a staggered difference-in-differences design (Callaway and Sant'Anna), with no pre-trends detected. A second design used a shift-share instrumental variable: monthly Copilot feature-release intensity times each worker's baseline share of collaborators already using Copilot. Findings: adoption was followed by more self-initiated collaboration hours (about 1.43 hours/month on average over the first three months), both synchronous and asynchronous; about 2.2 more collaborators (overall ATT); lower clustering; and more time concentrated on historically strong ties. The IV results pointed the same way.
script.limitations: The study covers a single business unit in one company, so results may not generalize to other industries or less interdependent jobs (e.g., software development). Data show who interacted and for how long, not what they discussed, so the proposed explanation (validating AI output) is not directly observed; alternatives include using saved time to interact or talking about the tool itself. Effects are measured only in the first three months after adoption. Causal claims rest on parallel-trends and instrument-validity assumptions; some overall ATT estimates were not statistically significant.

pt.title: IA no trabalho não isolou ninguém: mudou as equipes
pt.paper_title: IA generativa no trabalho e as redes de colaboração entre funcionários
pt.description: A Apple está colocando um chatbot de IA no Pages, no Keynote e no Numbers. Então, um assistente de IA no escritório faz a gente precisar menos dos colegas? Uma equipe da Universidade Bocconi analisou 13 meses de registros de reuniões, chamadas e e-mails de mais de 12.000 funcionários de uma multinacional durante a liberação gradual do Copilot. Quem adotou a IA colaborou mais, falou com mais colegas e se apoiou mais nos colegas de confiança. O estudo cobre uma única empresa e os três primeiros meses após a adoção.

scenes.heading: IA NO TRABALHO
scenes.big_text: Chegou a IA. E os colegas?
lines: A Apple pôs IA no Pages. Vai ficar mais solitário?
Dados de 12.000 trabalhadores deram uma resposta surpreendente.

scenes.heading: O ESTUDO
lines: Uma equipe da Universidade Bocconi publicou no arXiv em 2026.

scenes.heading: OS DADOS
lines: Acompanharam 12.000 funcionários de uma multinacional por 13 meses,
enquanto o assistente de IA Copilot era liberado aos poucos.

scenes.heading: COMO MEDIRAM
lines: Sem questionários, e sem ler o que as pessoas escreviam ou diziam.
Os registros mostraram o tempo em reuniões, chamadas, e-mails e chats.

scenes.heading: A REDE
lines: Uma hora juntos no mês já conta como uma ligação na rede.
Depois: quantos contatos, quão fechado o círculo, quanto de laços antigos?

scenes.heading: O TESTE
lines: Compararam 1.992 usuários de IA com 9.876 não usuários, antes e depois.
E conferiram de novo usando o momento dos lançamentos de novos recursos.

scenes.heading: O RESULTADO
lines: Depois da IA, colaboraram mais, com cerca de 2,2 contatos a mais.
Os círculos ficaram mais abertos, mas com mais apoio em colegas confiáveis.
Ressalva: uma empresa, três meses, e sem saber o que conversaram.

scenes.heading: CONCLUSÃO
scenes.big_text: A IA reorganizou o trabalho em equipe
lines: Aqui, a IA não deixou o trabalho mais solitário. Ela o reorganizou.
